findings.issue: _LAYER_ORDINAL refuses an ordinal layer phrase only when a clause-ending token follows (punctuation, end of text, 'because' or 'and'). Read against the task's invariant (refuse bottom/top/first/second/lowest/highest layer in prose, allow relational wording) this lets absolute claims through whenever any other word follows. I ran the pattern on these strings and it returned no match for each: 'The bottom layer holds only _output', 'This sits at the bottom layer of the table', 'the bottom layer is why it imports nothing', 'the bottom layer (see LAYERS)'. The lint therefore enumerates the continuations that make a claim absolute, the shape that let the numeral lint be beaten one wording at a time in earlier rounds. lmd9 pins eight refusal shapes, all of which end the clause, so nothing in the suite goes red for a hole of this shape.
findings.resolution: Invert the test: refuse every ordinal layer phrase and allow only a closed set of relational complements (a relative clause such as 'layer that/it/both/any/the three can reach', 'layer strictly above', 'layer it can occupy'). Add 'holds', 'is', 'of the' and a parenthesis to lmd9 as shapes that must be refused.

findings.issue: layer_mention_drift's docstring still lists only the word numeral, the L<N> spelling and the parenthesised number. It does not mention the ordinal arm that _layer_numerals now feeds into it. The refusal message says 'writes the layer numeral ... delete the number' for a phrase like 'the bottom layer', which has no number to delete, so the remedy sentence points a writer at the wrong repair.
findings.resolution: Add the ordinal arm to the docstring and give an ordinal hit its own message: say it is a position claim and name the relational rewrite, 'a layer above `_x`'.

findings.issue: The replacement heading 'WHY A LAYER ABOVE `_output` AND NO HIGHER' is still a claim about position, and no lint checks it. In _deps.LAYERS the three modules do not sit directly above `_output`: the _machine_paths/_excerpt row is between, and the modules are in the _manifest_io row (_deps.py:150-167). 'A layer above' reads as 'the next one up', and 'no higher' is an unverifiable ceiling that goes stale when a module is inserted. This is the stale-position class the task set out to close.
findings.resolution: State what the reasoning needs rather than a position: for example 'WHY THIS IMPORTS NOTHING BUT `_output`-level helpers, AND WHY EVERYTHING ARRIVES AS AN ARGUMENT', or name the layer-mate it must not import.

findings.issue: The two new prove-gates rows (lmd9 red row, lmd10 allow row) were never run. I confirmed that both anchors match exactly once, and that the planted red text '..., the bottom layer, for the collector' ends its clause with a comma. findings.resolution: Run `python3 tools/prove-gates.py` for these two rows from a committed tree (now that the commit exists) and record the outcome. The quick check is that the lmd9 row reports the lint firing and the lmd10 row reports lmd10 failing.
